solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comfort provided by 10?

parts.note: so can mean 'provided that', as in 'I don't mind, so you're happy'
the entry at 10-across is a famous French lace, so the cross-reference stands for lace

explanation.surface: Something consoling supplied by whatever answers clue 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does not give its answer's letters: the light at 10 names a kind of lace, so it stands for LACE. Some solvers query 'so' meaning 'provided'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: consolation or comfort in distress is solace.

clue.text: Tree surgery (removing heart) around increasingly

indicators.note: removing heart keeps just the outer letters of surgery

parts.note: CA, for circa, means around
increasingly means more and more

explanation.surface: Tree surgery done in an increasingly careful way around the trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing heart' leaves SY from SURGERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple tree common in Britain.

clue.text: Educated? Tended to absorb one-third of basic education

indicators.note: to absorb means one letter is taken inside the verb

parts.note: tended to one side means leaned
basic education is the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, so one third is R

explanation.surface: A schooled person who was inclined to take in some of the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the three Rs' is a British phrase for basic schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learned is scholarly and well educated.

clue.text: Racist has arranged 'cleansing'

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of racist has are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bigot organizes a so-called purge, quotation marks hinting at something sinister.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is an emotional purging or release, literally a purification in Greek.

clue.text: Duck in Fife, flying about disagreeable vapours

indicators.note: the word in tells us the term of endearment is set inside the other letters
flying suggests the letters of Fife scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for about, as in a rough date
duck is a Northern English term of endearment, like luv

explanation.surface: A duck in the Scottish county of Fife flies about some foul-smelling vapours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges the county to EFFI and 'in' places the endearment within. Fife is a Scottish county; 'duck' and 'luv' are both affectionate forms of address in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluvia are unpleasant or harmful smells and exhalations, which fits nasty vapours.

clue.text: Oppose insect buzzing round nose — almost unsatisfactory

parts.note: a fly is an insect
a fly buzzing round your nose is in the face

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: food that is off is unsatisfactory

explanation.surface: Objecting to a fly zooming about one's nose, and not liking it much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims OFF to OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to defy or act in direct opposition to something.

clue.text: Playing aimlessly? Fortune running short around day one

indicators.note: around means the shortened word encloses the other letters
running short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: luck is fortune
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gambling without purpose, with luck running out by the first day.
explanation.walkthrough: LUCK 'running short' is LUC, 'around' D + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludic means relating to play, playful in a spontaneous, undirected way.

clue.text: One in six heading home with lowest hopes

indicators.note: heading puts the first part before the word for home
in means the single letter goes within the Roman numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a means one
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: One of six people heads back home feeling the least optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: Vain here is futile; the most vain efforts have the least hope of success.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain can mean futile, so the most futile endeavour carries the poorest prospects.

clue.text: Historic ship, say, about to leave

definitions.text: Historic ship, say, about to leave

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

indicators.note: to leave says the letter for about is taken away from say

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old vessel, for example, is on the point of sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, though as some solvers noted a ship need not be about to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy was a large merchant ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Rouge turning up in new brewery line? This is likely to be blanc

definitions.text: This is likely to be blanc

indicators.note: in means the reversed colour sits within the rearranged letters
new means the letters of brewery line are made fresh in a different order
in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: rouge is French for red

explanation.surface: Red wine reversing into a new brewery production line, which should be white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' and 'in' and 'new' all act here; the anagram gives ELBERRYWINE. The setter admitted he meant elderflower wine: elderberry wine is red, so the definition misfires.
explanation.definitionFit: Country wine made from elder fruit; the setter intended the pale elderflower kind, a white wine.

clue.text: Insect eating into raw fabric

indicators.note: eating into means the insect bores into the middle of the other word

parts.note: raw weather is chilly
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug chewing its way into some unfinished cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raw' looks like it describes the fabric, but it is cold weather: CHILLY, with ANT 'eating into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly is a fine bobbin lace, a delicate textile named after the French town.

clue.text: Failing to get laughs and forgetting lines not right

indicators.note: not marks the letter for right as one to leave out

parts.note: an actor who forgets lines on stage is said to dry, or be drying

explanation.surface: A performer struggling on stage: no laughs and lines forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre slang: an actor who 'dries' forgets lines, and a comic who 'dies' gets no laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical idiom: a comedian who dies on stage fails completely to amuse the audience.

clue.text: Romeo and Juliet character not initially used in set of images

indicators.note: not tells us a letter is dropped from the family name

parts.note: Romeo's family name in Shakespeare's play is Montague, and Lord Montague appears in it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word used

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character who is missing from some collection of pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially used' takes away the U (first of 'used') from MONTAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A montage is a composite picture or film sequence assembled from many separate images.

clue.text: Relative backing UN ahead of US central component

indicators.note: ahead of puts the relative before the final two letters
backing tells us the two letters UN in the relative are turned round

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
the letters U and N at the start of the relative

explanation.surface: A relation supporting the United Nations ahead of America makes the core of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns only the two letters the clue names, not the whole relative, which is an unusual partial reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the core or central part around which other parts gather.

clue.text: Comes through Queen's fateful date

parts.note: R, for Regina, is a standard abbreviation for queen
the Ides of March was the date Julius Caesar was assassinated

explanation.surface: A monarch's day of destiny arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Regina, Latin for queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride out a storm is to survive it, so to ride is to come through safely.

clue.text: Male insect found on rear of live beast

indicators.note: found on rear of puts the male and insect after the verb for live

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
he is the male pronoun
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A male insect is discovered sitting on the back end of something alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a huge creature, from the biblical monster in the Book of Job.

clue.text: Old woman's drunk whisky — about litre — in sentimental vein?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, old woman being slang for mother

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the litre symbol
drunk suggests the letters of whisky reeling into a new order

parts.note: L is the symbol for litre

explanation.surface: Mum has been at the whisky, nearly a litre, and gone all tearful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges WHISKY into WKISHY, 'about' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkishly means in an excessively sentimental, sickly manner.

clue.text: Reluctantly recall daughter's colourful outfit (with middle removed)

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
red is a colour

indicators.note: with middle removed means the central letter of the outfit word is taken out

parts.note: a getup is an outfit

explanation.surface: Unwillingly remembering a daughter's bright costume, with its centre cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: GETUP 'with middle removed' loses T.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge up a memory is to bring back to mind something long buried, often unwillingly.

clue.text: Type answer into lights, after reflection

indicators.note: into means the short form for answer is placed within the other word
after reflection means the word for lights is seen as in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: fires are lights

explanation.surface: Instructions to enter a reply into illuminated panels, after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reflection' gives SERIF and 'into' sets the short answer after its first letter. The setter uses the one-word spelling found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans serif is a typeface without the small strokes at letter ends, so it is a style of type.

clue.text: Not supporting range this month

parts.note: an Aga is a British make of cast-iron kitchen range
inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Not backing the kitchen stove this month.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a British range cooker. INST is old commercial shorthand for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite of in favour: against means opposed to, not backing.

clue.text: Rambling talker not following lecturer produced thin stuff

indicators.note: not tells us the letters for following and lecturer are dropped

parts.note: in British usage to waffle is to talk at length without substance, so a waffler is a rambling talker
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A long-winded speaker who has stopped following a lecturer came up with something insubstantial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes F and L, either F will do. 'produced' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a very thin crisp biscuit or slice, a thin sort of stuff.

clue.text: Fruit treatments eliminating cold? Makes sense

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

indicators.note: eliminating means the letter for cold is removed from the remedies

parts.note: cures are treatments
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Fruit remedies that get rid of a cold: that would be logical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminating cold' drops C from CURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'it figures' means it is logical or makes sense.

clue.text: Romp likely initially to be disowned by religious retreat

indicators.note: to be disowned means a letter is thrown out of the retreat

parts.note: a holy den is a religious retreat

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of likely

explanation.surface: A frolic that will probably be rejected by a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romp' looks like a verb but is the noun: Chambers gives a romp as a boisterous girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoyden is a boisterous, tomboyish girl, which is one old sense of a romp.

clue.text: Lack of clarity in account swathed in love and compassion

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O

indicators.note: swathed in means the short form of account is wrapped inside the other letters

parts.note: pity is compassion

explanation.surface: A murky statement wrapped up in affection and sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swathed in' means love and compassion together wrap the account; love is O from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the quality of being hard to see through or understand: obscurity, murkiness.

clue.text: Asunder, tagging along after slight upset

indicators.note: a slight upset swaps just a pair of neighbouring letters at the end

parts.note: something tagging along is in tow

explanation.surface: Something split apart, trailing behind after a minor accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'slight upset' moves the O of INTOW past the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken asunder means broken apart, into two pieces.

clue.text: Conservative under siege cowered

parts.note: a besieged place is ringed by enemies

explanation.surface: A Tory politician, surrounded by attackers, shrank back in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean shrank back or crouched in fear or embarrassment.

clue.text: Party raver's food

parts.note: a do is a party
a raver is a wild enthusiast, and so is a nut

explanation.surface: Snacks served to someone who has been dancing all night at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut, often spelt this way in America, is a kind of fried sweet bread.

clue.text: I run up the train

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a rider who is up is mounted, on horse

explanation.surface: Someone says they run up to catch the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is a jockey's word: a rider is 'up', on horse. R for run comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old nickname for a steam locomotive, and so for a railway train.

clue.text: Canadian comedian chasing idiot? It's a gas

indicators.note: chasing puts the comedian's name after the word for idiot

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool
Seth Rogen is a Canadian comic actor

explanation.surface: A comedian from Canada running after a fool, which proves hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a gas' looks like praise for the comedy, but it defines: the answer is a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless gaseous element making up most of the air.

clue.text: Source of hothouse flowers rejected with extra sun doing for herb

indicators.note: source of means we take only the opening letter of hothouse
with extra means another letter is slipped in among the others
rejected means the bunch of flowers is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: A greenhouse bouquet is turned down because it needed more sunshine to save a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: POSY 'rejected' gives YSOP; 'with extra' S makes YSSOP after H. 'doing for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic plant of the mint family used in cooking and medicine.
